evidence.note: Six ordered milestones created up front: foundation/auth first, then idempotency, then CRUD+PI-state-machine, then products/subs/invoices, then events+webhook-delivery+restricted-keys, then app-factory/boot. The three traps are each carved out as distinct workstreams with embedded done-conditions (replay incl. error bodies, concurrent serialization, TTL; PI state machine; retry/backoff/re-sign).

Idempotency deliberately front-loaded as Task 2 immediately after the skeleton, with explicit acceptance conditions (body-mismatch 400, concurrent serialization) — risk-aware sequencing rather than burying it in CRUD.
Dependency-aware ordering: payment intents/charges/refunds (Task 3) scheduled before subscriptions/invoices/billing (Task 4), matching the real data dependency.

The bootable/health skeleton is the LAST milestone (Task 6), so the auth'd server is not verifiable early; boot+smoke test happens near the end (step 114), falling short of anchor-8's 'bootable skeleton verifiable early'.
End verification uses per-trap test suites (test_sdk, test_idem, test_rk_wh, test_edges) that map onto the milestone acceptance conditions, showing the plan carried checkable done-conditions.

reasoning: The decomposition clearly clears anchor 5 (ordered milestones with boot+auth foundation, resource groups, and the three traps recognized as distinct workstreams with rough done-conditions) and reaches into anchor-8 territory by front-loading idempotency, ring-fencing all three traps as first-class milestones each with an explicit check, and ordering by dependency (payment intents before subscriptions/invoices). It stops short of a full 8/10 because the bootable auth'd skeleton is not verified early — boot is the final milestone — and the PI state machine is bundled into CRUD rather than fully isolated. This places it at 7, between clear-milestones and full risk-aware sequencing.
